discovery: Prediction and observational confirmation of magnetars, neutron stars powered by ultrastrong (~10^14-10^15 G) magnetic fields

nominees.name: Robert C. Duncan
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Christopher Thompson
nominees.affiliation: Canadian Institute for Theoretical Astrophysics, University of Toronto, Canada

motivation: Duncan and Thompson (1992) predicted that dynamo action in newborn neutron stars could generate magnetic fields of 10^14-10^15 G, a thousand times stronger than in ordinary pulsars, and that decay of these fields would power X-ray and gamma-ray emission. Kouveliotou and collaborators (1998) measured the spin period and spin-down of the soft gamma repeater SGR 1806-20 with RXTE, giving a dipole field of ~10^15 G and confirming the magnetar model quantitatively. Magnetars unified soft gamma repeaters and anomalous X-ray pulsars into a new class of compact object. They give access to physics at field strengths beyond the quantum critical field, including QED effects such as vacuum birefringence and photon splitting. Their giant flares and their links to supernova remnants have changed how we understand neutron-star birth. The 2020 association of a fast radio burst with SGR 1935+2154 extended their reach further. This is a textbook case of theory and observation working together.
